{{Short description|French biologist (1920–2015)}}
'''Victor Marc Nigon''' (born 11 October 1920 in Metz, France, died 5 July 2015) was a biologist who was first to study the nematode worm ''[[Caenorhabditis elegans]]'' in the laboratory, with [[Ellsworth Dougherty]], in the 1940s.<ref>Les modalités de la reproduction et le determinisme du sexe chez quelques Nematodes libres. V Nigon - Annales de Sciences Naturelles-Zool. Biol. Anim., 1949</ref><ref>Reproductive patterns and attempts at reciprocal crossing of Rhabditis elegans maupas, 1900, and Rhabditis briggsae Dougherty and nigon, 1949 (Nematoda: Rhabditidae). Victor Nigon and Ellsworth C. Dougherty, JEZ-A Ecological and Integrative Physiology, Volume 112, Issue 3, December 1949, Pages 485–503, {{doi|10.1002/jez.1401120307}}</ref>

Jean-Louis Brun, a student of Nigon, continued experiments on the 'Bergerac' variety of ''C. elegans''.<ref>[http://www.wormbook.org/chapters/www_nematodeshistory/nematodeshistory.html History of research on C. elegans and other free-living nematodes as model organisms. Victor Marc Nigon and Marie-Anne Félix] at wormbook.org</ref>

The specific epithet given to the nematode species ''[[Caenorhabditis nigoni]]'' is a tribute to Victor Nigon.
